name: Nikhil Dubois

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms or government, and your answers stay confidential. What is a normal working day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I drive a haul truck at a large mine. Before the first run I check tyres, lights and the brake log, then I haul rock between the face and the crusher. I like solving a jam in the route with the other drivers; waiting for a dispatch screen to catch up with a wet ramp gets old.

say: I find **AI paperwork** helpful for finding entries, but I still check the manual.
I believe **haul trucks** need operators who know both the machine and the road.
think: I worry more about **mine costs** and rough shifts than mild AI change.
I know **three months** of savings is too small for careless bets.
do: **Test** the permitted report helper against my own inspection notes this month.
**Continue** driving the haul truck on scheduled shifts.
**Transfer** our usual monthly amount into savings before planning extras.
feel: **Calm** about limited AI change, with ordinary concern about the household cushion.
S0.quote: A fluent answer can still point to the wrong truck.
fieldNote: **Early tool use** does not mean blind trust; he checks outputs against the precise truck manual.
**Household discipline** is already in place through a monthly savings transfer and three months of expenses.

steps.text: Test the permitted inspection report helper against truck notes
Keep driving the haul truck on scheduled shifts
Transfer the usual monthly amount into household savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew the AI paperwork helper is useful for finding a missing inspection entry, but nobody should confuse it with a driver. I already use AI to sort manuals at home, then check the actual page before I touch a machine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A flat AI story still leaves us with the usual mine risks: fuel costs, rough shifts and a mortgage. I have about three months of expenses set aside. I am comfortable trying tools, but I cannot gamble that cushion on every idea.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep driving the haul truck and test the report helper on my own inspection notes this month, if the mine allows it. In the first year I would keep our monthly savings transfer and show my partner any change in overtime before we take on new costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Fairly calm about AI, though not completely relaxed about money. Three months of savings is a start, not a promise that everything is covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does checking the page mean?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a tool gives me a tyre-pressure number, I open the truck manual and check the model and load. A fluent answer can still point to the wrong truck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your partner notice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner would see the savings transfer arrive before we plan a weekend away. I do not want the children hearing us argue over an avoidable purchase.

say: I expect **office planning** to change first, while trucks still need judgment on live roads.
I want **dispatch tests** to include drivers who know closed ramps and poor routes.
think: I think **dispatch jobs** may shrink before haul truck shifts do.
I would consider **control-room work** if its paid shift rate supports our mortgage.
do: **Ask** dispatch to demonstrate its new scheduling tool this week.
**Record** wrong route suggestions with dates and road markers in the first year.
**Apply** for paid control-room training if the mine opens places and pay holds.
feel: **Anxious** about future truck shifts, yet curious enough to test dispatch tools early.
S1.quote: The mortgage means I cannot treat an unpaid experiment as a career plan.
fieldNote: **Field evidence** matters to him; he wants dated route errors, not general complaints about screens.
**Paid training** is conditional on the control-room rate, even though he enjoys trying new tools.
**Thinking tasks** reach dispatch first; his hands-on driving risk grows later with robots.

steps.text: Ask dispatch to demonstrate its scheduling tool this week
Record wrong mine routes with dates and road markers
Apply for paid control-room training if shift pay holds

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the office will feel this before the truck cab does. Better planning could stop us waiting in a line of vehicles, and I would volunteer to test the dispatch screen with the actual road conditions.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think fewer dispatch and buying jobs are likely if the software handles those tasks. Robots may follow more slowly, and a mine that learns to move trucks with fewer people will eventually test my job too. I want to be one of the people who understands the handover, if there is paid work in it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask dispatch to show me its new scheduling tool and keep a notebook of wrong route suggestions. In the first year I would apply for the mine's control-room training if it opens, while keeping my truck licence current.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about where the route leads, but curious enough to move first. The mortgage means I cannot treat an unpaid experiment as a career plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a wrong suggestion look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A screen could route a loaded truck toward a ramp closed after rain. I would record the date and road marker so dispatch can test the next version.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would moving into the control room reduce pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the shift rate before applying. If it meant a large pay cut, I would keep driving and learn the dispatch system from the cab instead.

say: I expect **2028 dispatch** change before capable truck robots around 2031.
I want **paid trials** to use drivers who know mine roads and blind spots.
think: I know **trial help** may teach the mine to run with fewer drivers.
I cannot cover a long hours cut with **three months** of savings.
do: **Request** paid access to autonomous-truck trials now and document safety faults.
**Take** a mine-funded control-room qualification after 2028 if there are no unpaid days.
**Apply** to two nearby mines for control jobs if truck shifts begin falling.
feel: **Anxious** about the short path from 2028 thinking AI to possible truck-robot shifts around 2031.
S2.quote: Three months of savings would vanish quickly against the mortgage.
fieldNote: **Volunteer instinct** persists, but he recognizes that teaching the mine may speed job cuts.
**Paid conditions** govern trial work and qualifications because the household has only three months of savings.
**Two dates** are kept separate: dispatch and inspection changes in 2028, driving risk around 2031.

steps.text: Join a paid autonomous-truck trial and document safety faults
Take a control-room qualification if the mine pays and no days are unpaid
Apply to two nearby mines if truck shifts begin falling

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my crew that full thinking AI by 2028 could rewrite dispatch and inspections long before a robot drives our trucks around 2031. We should get access to the trial data while human drivers still know every bad bend.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My first thought is to volunteer, but I know the mine might learn from us and then need fewer of us. If capable robots arrive around 2031, I could lose most of my driving hours. Three months of savings would vanish quickly against the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for paid access to any autonomous-truck trial and write down what safety faults I can spot. In the first year after 2028 I would take the control-room qualification if the mine pays for it, and send two applications to nearby mines with control jobs if our shifts start falling.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the speed, even while I want to see the machines work. Curiosity does not put dinner on the table if the truck roster collapses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would you tell at home first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my partner that 2028 is the office change and about 2031 is the truck change. We would look at the mortgage balance together before I accepted any training with unpaid days.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you refuse a safety trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would join a paid safety trial because I know the road and the blind spots. I would refuse to call it a job guarantee.

say: I think **2031 thinking AI** gives time to test dispatch before truck robots around 2034.
I can judge **control training** better while driving shifts remain available.
think: I could build **savings** with longer warning if overtime continues.
I suspect **nearby mines** may change together, limiting fallback jobs.
do: **Request** the control-room course schedule and pay scale this year.
**Add** about 25 monthly to savings if overtime holds.
**Shadow** a control operator on a paid shift after 2031 before applying.
feel: **Anxious** about a smaller driving role by 2034, with time for a measured move.
S3.quote: An interesting screen is not enough reason to miss a payment.
fieldNote: **Extra savings** is precisely limited to about 25 monthly and stops if overtime falls.
**Control-room interest** remains conditional on pay, course access and a paid shadow shift.
**Local jobs** are a fallback with a shared risk if nearby mines automate together.

steps.text: Add about 25 monthly to savings if overtime holds
Shadow a control operator on a paid shift after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the extra three years gives us a chance to test dispatch properly before 2031, then prepare for truck robots around 2034. I would rather learn the control desk while I still have a cab to go back to.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to thinking AI and about eight to robots changes the mortgage maths. I could build a larger cushion, provided our shifts hold, and make a real bid for control-room work. Nearby mines have some similar jobs, but they may all be making the same change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the training office this year for the control-room course schedule and the current pay scale. I would increase the monthly savings transfer by a small amount if overtime holds. In the first year after 2031 I would shadow a control operator on a paid shift and decide whether to apply.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious rather than alarmed. I still expect the driving role to be smaller by 2034, but I have time for a measured move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much more would you save?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We could add the price of one takeaway meal each month, about 25, without taking from school expenses. If overtime drops, that extra transfer stops.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make you stay in the cab?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the control role pays less than our mortgage budget can bear, I would stay while the truck shifts exist. An interesting screen is not enough reason to miss a payment.

say: I want **mine trials** to prove driverless trucks on real roads before shifts are replaced.
I expect **2036 dispatch** change before the possible 2039 change to truck driving.
think: I may have choices at **age 56** if the mortgage has fallen and children have finished school.
I cannot count on **retirement** without actual pension and mortgage figures.
do: **Renew** the truck operating certificate on time this year.
**Review** control-course fees and mortgage figures yearly with my partner.
**Test** AI dispatch on paid shifts after 2036 and seek control work if pay fits.
feel: **Uneasy** about eventual robots, while feeling steady about the next few years.
S4.quote: I would not tell the children I can retire until the mortgage and pension figures actually agree.
fieldNote: **Ten years** lets him plan training without assuming control work or retirement is guaranteed.
**Paid testing** remains his preferred way to learn dispatch tools after thinking AI arrives.
**Family costs** and mortgage balance anchor his yearly decision on course fees.

steps.text: Renew the truck operating certificate and keep driving
Test AI dispatch on paid mine shifts after 2036

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew there is enough time to make the mine prove any driverless system on our roads. Thinking AI reaches dispatch around 2036, but capable truck robots do not arrive until around 2039 in this picture.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2039 I would be 56, and my children might be through school. If the mortgage is smaller, I could choose a control job, fewer shifts or a different mine; I cannot know which will be open. I would keep learning rather than assume the last ten years will look like the first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would keep the truck work and renew my operating certificate on time. I would put a control-room course on a three-year plan, with a yearly check of fees and the mortgage. In the first year after 2036 I would test the AI dispatch system on paid shifts and apply for control work only if the rate suits us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, but mostly steady for the next few years. I can make several choices before a capable robot takes the wheel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens in that yearly check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner and I would compare the mortgage balance with savings and the children's school costs. If training fees have risen, we would delay the course rather than borrow for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you retire at 56?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know what our pension will cover then. I would not tell the children I can retire until the mortgage and pension figures actually agree.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most, because a 2031 robot truck would leave little time to change the mortgage budget. Paid access to trials and a real control-room qualification would help me use what I know about the road. I would also want clear pay rates before leaving the cab.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who gets to see the mistakes from the first truck trials. A driver can point out a blind bend, but the crew needs to hear whether anyone fixed it before shifts are removed.

headlineQuote: A driver can point out a blind bend, but the crew needs to hear whether anyone fixed it before shifts are removed.
portrait: **Nikhil, 43**, drives a haul truck and already uses AI to search manuals, then checks answers against the right machine.
**Three months** of savings, two school-age children and a mortgage put clear limits on unpaid experiments.
**Early testing** appeals to him; he wants dated road errors and paid access to driverless truck trials.
**Fast AGI** worries him because dispatch could change in 2028 and capable truck robots could follow around 2031.
**Longer warning** lets him weigh control-room training and a bigger cushion, always against actual pay and family costs.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** gives the shortest path from changed dispatch work to possible loss of driving shifts around 2031.
whatWouldHelp: **Paid trial access** and a control-room qualification would let him test machines and use his road knowledge.
**Clear pay rates** would help him decide whether a control job can cover the mortgage.
